title: EXO: Accelerating Storage Paravirtualization with eBPF
problem: KVM/QEMU-based paravirtualization incurs multiple context switches for guest I/O requests, creating non-negligible software overhead with modern fast NVMe storage devices.
motivation: Reducing I/O path overhead is critical for applications leveraging high-performance storage in virtualized environments.
method: EXO extends virtio-blk with an eBPF-based in-kernel fast path that directly queries guest-to-host address mappings without switching to the user-space QEMU backend. The original virtio-blk slow path is preserved as a fallback for complex operations requiring full backend processing.
key_novelty: Using eBPF to implement an in-kernel fast path for virtio-blk that bypasses user-space backend processing by directly handling guest-to-host address mapping queries.
contributions: eBPF-based in-kernel fast path for virtio-blk storage paravirtualization avoiding context switches
Hybrid approach preserving fallback to full QEMU backend for complex operations
Performance competitive with or exceeding existing storage paravirtualization solutions

metrics.speedup: similar or higher than existing storage paravirtualization solutions

primary_theme: In-kernel eBPF fast path for storage paravirtualization
